title: Saviour of the Sin-sick Soul
description: Saviour of the Sin-sick Soul in Tonic Solfa to VIENNA, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 398.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Sevens (7.7.7.7), and this page sets them to VIENNA; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Sa-viour of the sin sick soul, Give me faith to make me whole! Fin-ish thy great work of grace, Cut it short in right-eous-ness.

lines: Give me faith to make me whole!
Finish thy great work of grace,
Cast it out by perfect love.
None but Christ to me be given!
None but Christ in earth or heaven.
O that I might now decrease!
O that all I am might cease!
Let my Lord be all in all!

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to VIENNA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
